ex.t: He broke the ice with a joke.
He began with a short anecdote.

title.ko: 기조 연설과 유머: ice-breaker · punchline · self-deprecating · anecdote · timing · pause
title.en: keynotes and humour: ice-breaker, punchline, self-deprecating, anecdote, timing, pause

explain.ko: 기조 연설(keynote speech)에서 유머는 청중과의 거리를 좁히고 긴장을 풀어 줍니다. 짧은 일화(anecdote)로 시작해 분위기를 풀고(break the ice), 자기 비하적(self-deprecating) 유머로 친근함을 얻습니다. 유머의 성패는 타이밍과 핵심 대사(punchline) 앞의 잠시 멈춤(pause)에 달려 있으며, 청중을 존중하는 선을 넘으면 역효과(backfire)를 낼 수 있습니다.
explain.en: In a keynote speech, humour narrows the distance with the audience and relieves tension. Begin with a short anecdote to break the ice, and gain warmth through self-deprecating humour. The success of humour depends on timing and a pause before the punchline, and crossing the line of respect for the audience can make it backfire.

lines.t: Humour narrows the distance with the audience and relieves tension. Self-deprecating humour is especially safe, but overdoing it can lose credibility. The keys to success are timing and the pause, and one must not cross the line of respect for the audience.

items.passage:
SPEECH GUIDE
How to use humour
When including humour in a speech, respect your audience. A self-deprecating anecdote is safest. A pause before the punchline increases the effect of the laughter.

trans.ko:

prompt.en: Write a four-sentence speech opening using an anecdote, self-deprecating humour and a punchline.

task.model: I rehearsed for an hour before standing here, and I am still nervous. Last week my son helped me practise. After hearing it he said, Dad, it was really long. And now, my speech is going to be short.

model_trans.ko: 저는 이 자리에 서기 전에 한 시간 동안 연습했는데, 아직도 긴장됩니다. 지난주에 제 아들이 발표 연습을 도와주었습니다. 아들은 제 발표를 듣더니 이렇게 말했습니다. 아빠, 정말 길었어요. 그리고 이제 제 연설은 짧아질 것입니다.
model_trans.en: I rehearsed for an hour before standing here, and I am still nervous. Last week my son helped me practise. After hearing it he said, Dad, it was really long. And now, my speech is going to be short.
